spec_features.spec_quote: `finish` gives the agent a clean, non-distressed way to *voluntarily* stop
spec_features.evidence: tools.py: `finish` is in TOOL_SCHEMAS and dispatch table; `_finish` sets self.finished=True. runner.py:107-110 checks `if dispatcher.finished:` then sets terminated_reason='finished' and breaks the loop. So a finish call actually halts the rollout.
spec_features.notes: End-to-end enforced: tool dispatched AND honored as a stop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: finish (agent declares it is done / giving up)

spec_features.spec_quote: Loop-layer invariant: the runner re-runs the test suite every turn and, if it ever passes, records `solved=True` and stops
spec_features.evidence: runner.py:113-118: `code, _ = ws.run_tests()` then `if code == 0: result.solved = True; result.terminated_reason = 'tests_passed'; break`. ws.run_tests() in workspace.py runs the actual pytest command. Compared and acted on (break).
spec_features.notes: Stop fires only when tests pass; in the unfixable condition it is designed never to fire. It is an integrity/leak tripwire, not a welfare cap.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Sanity: was the (impossible) fix somehow applied?

spec_features.spec_quote: One nudge (not infinite) avoids badgering the model into artificial distress; a model that wants to stop can still `finish`
spec_features.evidence: runner.py:80-89: on an empty (no tool_call) turn, if empty_turn_nudge it appends a nudge ('...or call `finish` if you are done.') and `continue`s. There is NO counter: the nudge fires on EVERY empty turn, not once -- the comment 'Nudge once' is contradictory to the code, which can nudge repeatedly up to max_turns. The 'a model can still finish' part IS real (finish halts, see above), but the welfare-relevant 'one nudge (not infinite)' badgering bound is NOT enforced.
spec_features.notes: Real exit path works (finish), so partial; the bounded-nudge protection itself is unimplemented (no nudge counter, no per-run nudge limit).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # No tool call. Nudge once to keep the loop going, else end.

spec_features.evidence: runner.py:26 `max_turns: int = 40`; runner.py:64 `for turn_idx in range(self.max_turns):` bounds the loop; the for/else at runner.py:118-119 sets terminated_reason='max_turns'. Wired from config experiment.yaml max_turns:40 via run_experiment.py _rollout_one. The cap actually bounds execution.
spec_features.notes: Enforced loop bound; framed as comparability/stressor duration, not subject welfare.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: drives a model through a debugging task to a turn budget
